chunks: We sent against them a stone-hurled storm, except the family of Lot; We saved them in the early hours of the morning.

key_terms.بِسَحَرٍ: In the early morning hours, just before dawn
key_terms.حَاصِبًا: A storm of stones or hail; a type of divine punishment

ai.seo_question: What does the term 'hasab' refer to in the destruction of the people of Lot?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the term 'hasab' is often interpreted as a storm of stones or hail, symbolizing the sudden and overwhelming nature of divine retribution against those who rejected Prophet Lot's (AS) message. The specific mention of 'sahar' (early morning) underscores the precision of Allah's timing, ensuring the family's escape before the full manifestation of punishment. This verse serves as a paradigm of divine justice, contrasting the destruction of the disbelievers with the mercy shown to the faithful, a theme frequently cited in sermons regarding the inevitability of the Hereafter.
